a2-unit-03.03.1 Podcast:
Host: Welcome to Green City, the podcast about nature in New York. Today I'm not in the studio. I'm walking in the North Woods, a forty-acre woodland in the north of Central Park. My guide is a Brazilian photographer who lives here now. He's a tour guide too, and every Saturday he takes visitors on a very slow walk. Hi Paulo!
Paulo: Hi! Thanks for having me. And welcome to my favorite place in the city.
Host: So what are we doing today?
Paulo: We're forest bathing. The idea comes from Japan, where people call it shinrin-yoku. It just means time with the trees. There are no rules. You walk slowly, you breathe and you use your five senses.
Host: I love that idea. In New York everybody walks fast!
Paulo: I know. That's why I think the city needs this. OK, let's start with our eyes. I'm looking at this old oak tree. What do you see?
Host: It looks enormous! The trunk is really thick, and the branches go up to the sky. The leaves are turning orange and red.
Paulo: That's right. It's October, so the colors change every week. Now close your eyes. What do you hear?
Host: I'm listening very carefully... I hear water. And birds. It sounds so peaceful. I can't believe we're in Manhattan!
Paulo: That water is the Loch, a small stream. It runs through the woods to a lake called the Harlem Meer. Now take a leaf and smell it.
Host: I'm smelling it now... It smells fresh, like rain. And the ground smells a little sweet.
Paulo: Now touch the bark of this tree.
Host: OK, I'm touching it. It feels rough and cold. And this moss feels soft, like a carpet!
Paulo: In Brazil I always did this with my grandmother Lourdes. She has a mango tree in her yard, and the mangoes taste so sweet!
Host: There's no fruit here today. But this apple from my bag tastes great!
Paulo: Ha! That works too. So how do you feel now?
Host: I feel much calmer. Honestly, I understand why people come back every week. I want to do this again.
Paulo: Most people say the same thing. You don't need a big forest in the mountains. You only need some trees and some time.
Host: That's all for today. For information about the Saturday walks, visit our website. See you next week on Green City!
